text:
maria: Heads-up — we're rolling forward the RBAC split for the backup-uploader role tomorrow (split into uploader-write + uploader-read). Wanted to surface two risks: 1) existing restores use ephemeral KMS grants tied to the old role, 2) our staging canary still accepts objects without SSE-C/A metadata.
aj: thanks — do we have a migration plan for KMS grants? if we rotate role name the grant principal changes.
maria: not fully. current plan was to create a short-lived grant for the new role and update restore jobs. but worried we missed some agents that request grants using the serviceaccount email.
sam: quick sanity check — how many live snapshots reference the old role in metadata? I can grep audit logs.
claire: also discovered yesterday in a vuln scan: the legacy backup-agent writes intermediate .sql.gz.tmp files to /tmp with 0644 until upload completes. possible cleartext window if the uploader fails.
devansh: yikes. that's a much higher severity for compliance. can we change the agent to use secure tmp (O_EXCL + 0600) and atomic rename?
claire: yes, patch is trivial. but rollout needs care — agent image used in both hosted and dedicated fleets.
maria: priority matrix: patch agent (hotfix), add S3 bucket policy to reject non-SSE uploads (short term), enforce KMS grant migration (medium). thoughts?
aj: +1 on S3 policy — reduce blast radius immediately. policy snippet I tested: `Condition: { "StringNotEquals": { "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms" } }` with Deny. we should scope to uploader role.
sam: I'll run an audit for objects missing `x-amz-server-side-encryption` and list keys uploaded in last 7 days. quick grep: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket prod-backups --query 'Contents[?LastModified>=`2024-12-01`].Key'` then `aws s3api head-object --bucket prod-backups --key <key>` to check SSE headers.
claire: also found one restore job that uses a long-lived KMS grant (no TTL) created by hand in 2023 — that needs revoking and replaced with a grant-for-restore flow.
devansh: for the migration: plan to create new cmk grant for `uploader-write` with TTL 1h, update restore tooling to request an on-demand grant via encops service, and revoke remaining grants with audit. we should add a canary that attempts a decrypt with revoked grant to assert failure.
maria: canops checklist: 1) hotfix backup-agent (O_EXCL + 0600 + unlink on error) 2) staged rollout to canary fleet 3) apply bucket deny-non-sse for prod-backups 4) scan last-30d for unencrypted keys and re-encrypt/reattach metadata 5) create new short-lived KMS grants and update restore jobs 6) revoke old grants and rotate service account creds 7) postmortem + external audit note.
aj: for #4 — we can't re-encrypt server-side if object was uploaded without SSE-KMS, we need to download and re-upload with proper headers or use S3 Copy with SSE-KMS if provider supports. please add that detail to runbook.
sam: on the scan I already found ~12 objects without SSE header, mostly small dev snapshots. tagging them now into a ticket.
claire: patch branch: `fix/secure-tempfile` created, PR up. also added unit that fails if file permissions are wider than 0600.
encops-bot: ALERT: staging uploader fleet shows 3 failed uploads in past hour — root cause: transition test for role split returned AccessDenied for one job (serviceaccount not updated).
devansh: seeing that — rolling back the canary role update for staging. need to ensure grant bridge is available before we flip prod.
maria: action owners: claire -> hotfix PR and canary rollout (ETA 2h), sam -> audit listing + remediation ticket (ETA 3h), aj -> S3 bucket policy + prod deny staging -> I'll coordinate with infra (ETA 1h), devansh -> KMS grant script + revoke plan (ETA 4h).
aj: will also add CloudTrail filter to capture `Grant*` KMS events and `PutObject` without SSE to the incident channel. use `aws logs filter` rule I posted earlier.
sam: note — we should not mass-revoke grants until we've validated active restores with the new flow. create a small rollout window and monitor `Decrypt` errors.
claire: PR description includes migration steps and a healthcheck: `find /tmp -type f -name "*.tmp" -mtime -1 -exec stat -c "%n %a" {} \;` to detect wide perms.
maria: good. once we patch and enforce S3 policy, we should run a single controlled reupload of one affected snapshot to confirm copy + SSE-KMS preserves accessibility. add smoke test to restore pipeline.
devansh: I'll prepare the KMS grant rotation script: create grant -> record grantId in secret-store -> update job to use grantId -> after successful restore cycles revoke by grantId. automation will include TTL fallback.
encops-bot: NOTE: created ticket SEC-2026 for unencrypted-uploads + uploaded objects list. assigned to @sam and @aj.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: canary-run queued for `backup-agent:fix-secure-tempfile` -> will run after manual approval.
maria: thanks all. after hotfix + S3 policy live, we'll schedule an incident review and propose an audit entry for compliance. keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
